comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
KOEI has the final say in all matters. NetMarble and OGP were/are little more than chauffeurs; they had/have a bit of authority, but not nearly so much as you suppose. The idea that a company would invest time and money into resurrecting a server from scratch after it failed them once before, is also entirely unrealistic -- KOEI is far more likely to say, 'Well, we gave it a go, but experiment over; no more International servers that are free-to-play'.

There is also the fact that a complete reset would alienate a ton of players, veteran or otherwise; I personally would be heartbroken to see all my work gone in the blink of an eye, and I doubt very much too many of us would stick around to help the 'new generation', likely dooming this supposed 'fresh start server' to digital oblivion as well.

Am I disappointed in some of the choices made by the powers that be, and that certain things are not available in UWO? Sure. But I remain grateful to have a game available to play at all. UWO is incredibly niche; I never thought it would make it out of the East Asian gaming sphere. Oh, and for a supposedly 'dead' game, I notice that today's maintenance is coinciding with the announcement for the next expansion. Which happens to be Atlantis, if I'm not very much mistaken.

Now. I am not against a civil discussion of these and other points, but I would suggest that UWODB is not the place for them. This database is meant to collect game information and strategies. I'd rather things like 'our hosting service stinks / this player's bad / dead game even though players can suggest and organize their own events (never saw that with NM) / etc.' be spoken of elsewhere. It's not what people come here to see. Thanks for your consideration.

Cheers, and good voyaging online to you.

comments.author: BIakeC
comments.body:
I did know someone that moved to the Taiwanese Server. He had to get someone over there to make an account for him and use their info to log in (phone number has to match the dial code for Taiwan, etc). I'm not sure how he handled making payments since it's P2P server, among other issues, but I heard back it ended being a lot more work then he expected. Language barriers can also be an issue since they will only address you in their native tongue (Korean, Mandarin, etc) and im sure they wont take too kindly having an "outsider" play on their server if they found out.

That being said, I would hardly call UWO on GAMA P2W. There are many so called P2W games out there that come to a slowing crawl or halt unless you fork out money that can go up to the hundreds (and sometimes thousands) if your not careful. Up until fairly recently, I bought very NM currency, and later astros, save for the occasional SSIP and NPCs, and I did just fine. Those items from the astros shop, can make the game a little bit easier, but their not overall needed.

However I do wish that OGplanet could do a better job on handling UWO. For starters, they need to make the sailors bottle drop more useful stuff more often, and have the astros ships drop at a bit better rate as well. This would not only encourage players to buy the sailors bottle more often, but it would make ships and premium equipment cheaper so players that cant (or wont) buy from sailors bottle can purchase these equipment without having to go to the poor house.

comments.author: El_Dorito
comments.body:
Google gamecity jp if you're interested in playing on the Japanese server. I didn't spend a lot of time there but I was never banned with a US IP. Unless things have changed you can sign up for a 1 week free trial and have a look around.

@BlakeC You might be interested in the psychology involved in designing these "f2p" lottery systems. OGP makes more money when they offer less. It's in their interest to keep drops extremely rare and exclusive. If they didn't power users would get what they want relatively quickly and stop spending. Keep rates low and the sky is the limit as to what you can siphon out of certain people. If you're spending 20 - 30 USD every month on GAMA you aren't even a blip on their radar, they're hunting whales and won't change anything as long as 1% of players are willing to spend a few hundred USD every couple weeks on their lottery bottles.
